stem: Which of the following best describes the anatomical location and pathophysiology of bronchiolitis?

options.text: Inflammation of the larynx and trachea causing subglottic narrowing
Inflammation and oedema of the airways approximately two-thirds down the bronchial tree causing narrowing
Inflammation of the alveoli causing consolidation
Chronic narrowing of the large airways due to structural abnormalities
Inflammation of the pleura causing pleuritic pain

explanation: Bronchiolitis is inflammation and oedema of the small airways in the lower bronchial tree, leading to airway narrowing and obstruction.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because inflammation of the larynx and trachea with subglottic narrowing describes croup rather than bronchiolitis.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because bronchiolitis affects the small airways approximately two-thirds down the bronchial tree, where inflammation and oedema narrow the bronchioles.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because alveolar inflammation with consolidation describes pneumonia, not bronchiolitis.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because chronic narrowing due to structural abnormality describes a chronic large-airway disorder, not an acute viral bronchiolar inflammation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because pleural inflammation causes pleurisy and pleuritic pain, not the small-airway obstruction seen in bronchiolitis.

source.hint: Consider the specific part of the bronchial tree mentioned in the definitions and the resulting physical changes.
